sources.note: Spends test-time compute on iteratively refining each sampled rollout rather than on drawing more of them, then majority-votes the refined answers, with no verifier.
sources.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Bolts a small trainable recurrent block between a frozen 1.1B language model's body and its output head, so reasoning happens as repeated refinement of two latent vectors rather than as generated tokens.
sources.title: Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework

sources.note: Finds that a reasoning model's first solution is usually its best and that later alternatives are actively harmful, characterizes the errors as a forest structure, and prunes accordingly.
sources.title: FoE: Forest of Errors Makes the First Solution the Best in Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Identifies double-checking after the correct answer is already derived as 'invalid thinking', and trains a GRPO variant with a compress reward that targets exactly that portion.
sources.title: Optimizing Length Compression in Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Verifies correctness without training by comparing a reasoning trace's start-to-end hidden-state delta against two class centroids built from labelled experience.
sources.title: Your Reasoning Model is Secretly a Reward Model - Optimization-Free Verification from Experience

sources.note: Finds diffusion language models are badly miscalibrated on math reasoning yet rank correct from incorrect far better than autoregressive baselines, because their confidence tracks structural consistency rather than correctness.
sources.title: The Confidence Paradox: Unveiling the Latent Discriminative Power of Diffusion Large Language Models in Mathematical Reasoning

sources.note: Defines certaindex, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and builds it into a serving system that reallocates or terminates compute per query — saving up to 50% of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput.
sources.title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex

sources.note: Shows that CoT entropy follows a two-phase structure — a high-entropy exploration region that shifts abruptly into a low-entropy convergence region — and detects that shift online with the CUSUM change-point algorithm to drive early exit and trajectory-weighted voting.
sources.title: Unveiling the Entropy Dynamics of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

sources.note: Stops self-consistency sampling by Bayesian posterior over which answer is the mode, and proves that tracking only the top two answer counts plus an aggregate is enough for asymptotic optimality.
sources.title: Optimal Bayesian Stopping for Efficient Inference of Consistent LLM Answers

sources.note: Recasts when-to-stop-reasoning as optimal stopping rather than classification, and proves that a fixed threshold on the probability of being correct can be arbitrarily far from optimal even when that probability is known exactly, because the decision needs the value of continuing and not the value of stopping.
sources.title: OS-Pruner: Pruning Chains-of-Thought of Reasoning Models via Optimal Stopping

result.definition: How much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and across 10 sources the signal several archived systems use to decide when to stop spending. Its clearest formulation is algorithm-agnostic and built into a serving system, saving up to 50 percent of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput by reallocating or terminating per query. Two findings complicate the simple reading that convergence means correctness. A model's first solution is usually its best and later alternatives are actively harmful in one study, which structures the errors as a forest and prunes accordingly -- so continued generation past stabilisation is not neutral. And double-checking after the correct answer has already been derived is identifiable as a distinct portion of a trace and targetable by a compression reward. Against those, the archive's calibration material bounds what stabilisation licenses: uniformly high confidence across a trace indicates a failure to branch rather than a well-supported answer, and in the highest-agreement bin the plurality is correct about half the time on hard problems. One source finds a model family badly miscalibrated yet ranking correct from incorrect well, because its confidence tracks structural consistency rather than correctness -- which is stabilisation and correctness coming apart explicitly.
